newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bond prices ended mixed with prices in the short end slightly lower while the longer maturities were able to move back towards recent highs.

The December confederate bond futures contract closed in once again on the October 9 contract high of 115.80, moving up to a day session peak of 115.64. Meanwhile March three-month EuroSwiss traded on LIFFE eased back slightly, but one trader said the tone even in the short end was positive in view of the Swiss franc's latest declines versus the mark. The mark on Thursday put in a new 20-month high, rising to 84.43 centimes. This was just above the high set last Friday of 84.37.

The Swiss franc's declines last week triggered sharp rises in Swiss short-term rates, but the impact may have been lessened this week, amidst belief the Swiss National Bank is will to act to offset any upward pressure on short-term rates.
The SNB, as expected, left its discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent after today's regular weekly meeting of its three-man board.

Traders said caution was in order after the latest gains in the long end. "The risk is that we could see a sharp rise. We could see 116.00 and 116.50 (on the December futures contract). And then we look for our parachutes," one head dealer said.
Dec Comi medium-term bond down four at 110.11
March Euro Swiss francs down three at 97.78.
